match.reason: None of the bank points teaches solving differential equations by separating variables; they cover simultaneous equations, optimisation, correlation and scatterplots, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Separation of variables
card: A differential equation of the form dy/dx = f(x) × g(y) can be solved by separating the variables. Get all the y terms on one side with dy, and all the x terms on the other with dx.
Then integrate both sides: ∫ 1/g(y) dy = ∫ f(x) dx. Put a single constant c on one side only, as the two constants combine into one.
Use a given point to find c, then solve for y if the question asks for it.
dy/dx = 2xy, with y = 1 when x = 0. Separate: ∫ 1/y dy = ∫ 2x dx, so ln y = x² + c. Putting in x = 0, y = 1 gives 0 = 0 + c, so c = 0. Then y = e^(x²).
draft.remember: Put y with dy and x with dx, integrate both sides, then use the point to find c.

a.q: Which line is the correct first step in separating dy/dx = 3y²x?
a.why: Dividing both sides by y² and multiplying by dx puts all the y terms with dy and all the x terms with dx. This gives 1/y² dy = 3x dx. Multiplying by y² instead, as in the second option, would leave y on the wrong side.
a.clue: Divide by whatever y expression multiplies dx.

b.q: Solve dy/dx = 2y, given y = 3 when x = 0. What is y when x = ln 2?
b.why: Separating gives ∫ 1/y dy = ∫ 2 dx, so ln y = 2x + c. Then c = ln 3, so y = 3e^(2x). At x = ln 2, y = 3e^(2 ln 2) = 3 × 4 = 12. The answer 6 comes from treating e^(2 ln 2) as 2.

problems.detail: The why refers to 'the second option', but options are shown in random order, so this position may not match what students see. It also says multiplying by y² gives ∫ y² dy = ∫ 3x dx, which is wrong: multiplying both sides by y² gives y² dy/dx = 3y⁴x. That option comes from leaving y² with dy without dividing.

The example writes ∫ 1/y dy = ln y. The general result is ln|y| + c, as expected in VCE Specialist. Dropping the modulus is only justified here because y = 1 > 0, and the card does not say so. Students may learn to omit the absolute value.

check.summary: Both questions are correct (answers ∫ 1/y² dy = ∫ 3x dx and 12). Two small issues: the why for (a) refers to an option by position and misdescribes how the distractor arises, and the card writes ln y without the modulus or any note on why it can be dropped.

proposal.title: Separation of variables
card: A differential equation of the form dy/dx = f(x) × g(y) can be solved by separating the variables. Get all the y terms on one side with dy, and all the x terms on the other with dx.
Then integrate both sides: ∫ 1/g(y) dy = ∫ f(x) dx. Note that ∫ 1/y dy = ln|y|. Put a single constant c on one side only, as the two constants combine into one.
Use a given point to find c. If y > 0 at that point, ln|y| can be written as ln y. Then solve for y if the question asks for it.
dy/dx = 2xy, with y = 1 when x = 0. Separate: ∫ 1/y dy = ∫ 2x dx, so ln|y| = x² + c. At x = 0, y = 1, so c = 0. As y > 0, ln y = x², so y = e^(x²).
proposal.remember: Put y with dy and x with dx, integrate both sides, then use the point to find c.

a.q: Which line is the correct first step in separating dy/dx = 3y²x?
a.why: Dividing both sides by y² gives (1/y²) dy/dx = 3x, so 1/y² goes with dy and 3x with dx. Writing ∫ y² dy = ∫ 3x dx leaves y² with dy without dividing by it, so the equation is no longer the same.
a.clue: Which operation moves y² off the x side?

b.q: Solve dy/dx = 2y, given y = 3 when x = 0. What is y when x = ln 2?
b.why: Separating gives ∫ 1/y dy = ∫ 2 dx, so ln|y| = 2x + c, and c = ln 3. As y > 0, y = e^(2x + ln 3) = 3e^(2x). At x = ln 2, y = 3e^(ln 4) = 3 × 4 = 12. The answer 6 comes from treating e^(2 ln 2) as 2.
b.clue: e^(a + b) = e^a × e^b, and 2 ln 2 = ln 4.
